concept.concept_description: Formalize the Cramér random model of primes and prove it predicts the Prime Number Theorem. The Cramér model is a probabilistic model where each integer n ≥ 2 is independently declared a 'random prime' with probability 1/ln(n). Part 1 (deterministic): Define cramerSum(x) = Σ_{n=2}^{⌊x⌋} 1/ln(n) and prove the asymptotic cramerSum(x) ~ x/ln(x) as x → ∞, establishing that the expected count of random primes satisfies PNT. Part 2 (probabilistic): Define the product probability space on {0,1}^ℕ with independent Bernoulli(1/ln(n)) marginals. Define the random counting function π_C(ω,x) = |{n ∈ [2,x] : ω_n = 1}|. Prove: (a) E[π_C(x)] = cramerSum(x), (b) Var[π_C(x)] ≤ cramerSum(x) by independence of the Bernoulli variables, (c) PNT holds in probability: for any ε > 0, P(|π_C(x)/cramerSum(x) - 1| > ε) → 0 as x → ∞ via Chebyshev's inequality. This gives a rigorous formal foundation for 'counterfactual number theory' showing that PNT survives in the random model.

## Definitions Required

1. `cramerSum (x : ℝ) : ℝ` := Σ n in Finset.Icc 2 ⌊x⌋₊, (1 : ℝ) / Real.log n
   The expected count of random primes up to x.

2. `CramerModel` : A product probability space on ℕ → {0,1} where the n-th coordinate (for n ≥ 2) follows Bernoulli(1/ln(n)) independently.

3. `cramerCount (ω : CramerModel) (x : ℝ) : ℕ` := |{n ∈ [2, ⌊x⌋] : ω n = true}|
   The random prime counting function.

## Theorems to Prove

### Part 1: Deterministic Asymptotics

`lemma cramerSum_integral_bound {x : ℝ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) :
  (∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, (1 : ℝ) / Real.log t) - 1 ≤ cramerSum x ∧
  cramerSum x ≤ (∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, (1 : ℝ) / Real.log t) + 1`

Compare the sum to the logarithmic integral via Euler's sum-integral comparison.

`lemma cramerSum_asymptotic :
  cramerSum =ᶠ[atTop] fun x => x / Real.log x`

Prove cramerSum(x) ~ x/ln(x) as x → ∞. Strategy: show cramerSum(x) = Li(x) + O(1) where Li(x) = ∫₂ˣ dt/ln(t), then use the known asymptotic Li(x) ~ x/ln(x) + x/(ln x)² + ....

### Part 2: Probabilistic Concentration

`lemma cramerCount_expectation (x : ℝ) (hx : 2 ≤ x) :
  E[cramerCount · x] = cramerSum x`

By linearity of expectation and independence.

`lemma cramerCount_variance (x : ℝ) (hx : 2 ≤ x) :
  Var[cramerCount · x] ≤ cramerSum x`

Since Var(sum of independent Bernoullis) = sum of p_n(1-p_n) ≤ sum of p_n = cramerSum.

`theorem cramer_PNT_in_probability (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    P[|cramerCount · x - cramerSum x| ≥ ε * cramerSum x] ≤ 1 / (ε² * cramerSum x)`

By Chebyshev's inequality. Since cramerSum x → ∞, the probability → 0.

`theorem cramer_PNT :
  ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    P[|cramerCount · x / (x / Real.log x) - 1| > ε] = 0 ∨
    P[|cramerCount · x / (x / Real.log x) - 1| > ε] < ε`

The PNT holds in probability in the Cramér model.

/-
  Flag complexes and clique complexes of simple graphs
  ====================================================

  This file formalizes the equivalence between flag complexes and clique
  complexes of simple graphs.

  An abstract simplicial complex `K` is a *flag complex* iff a finite set of
  vertices is a face of `K` exactly when all of its distinct pairs are edges of
  the 1-skeleton of `K`.  The clique complex of a graph `G` is the simplicial
  complex whose faces are the cliques of `G`.  The main results show that the
  clique complex of any graph is flag, and that an abstract simplicial complex
  is flag if and only if it equals the clique complex of its own 1-skeleton.
-/
import Mathlib

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]

/-- An abstract simplicial complex on `α`. -/
structure ASC (α : Type*) where
  /-- The set of faces of the complex. -/
  faces : Set (Finset α)
  /-- Faces are downward closed: every subset of a face is a face. -/
  down_closed : ∀ s ∈ faces, ∀ t ⊆ s, t ∈ faces
  /-- Every vertex appearing in some face is itself a (singleton) face. -/
  singletons_mem : ∀ a, (∃ s ∈ faces, a ∈ s) → ({a} : Finset α) ∈ faces

/-- The 1-skeleton of an abstract simplicial complex: vertices `a` and `b` are
adjacent precisely when `a ≠ b` and `{a, b}` is a face. -/
def oneSkel (K : ASC α) : SimpleGraph α :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun a b => ({a, b} : Finset α) ∈ K.faces)

/-- Characterisation of adjacency in the 1-skeleton. -/
@[simp]
lemma oneSkel_adj (K : ASC α) (a b : α) :
    (oneSkel K).Adj a b ↔ a ≠ b ∧ ({a, b} : Finset α) ∈ K.faces := by
  unfold oneSkel
  rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, h | h⟩
    · exact ⟨hne, h⟩
    · exact ⟨hne, by rwa [Finset.pair_comm] at h⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩
    exact ⟨hne, Or.inl h⟩

/-- The 1-skeleton relation is symmetric. -/
lemma oneSkel_symm (K : ASC α) : Symmetric (oneSkel K).Adj := (oneSkel K).symm

/-- The 1-skeleton relation is irreflexive. -/
lemma oneSkel_irrefl (K : ASC α) (a : α) : ¬ (oneSkel K).Adj a a := (oneSkel K).irrefl

/-- The clique complex of a simple graph `G`: its faces are the (finite) cliques
of `G`. -/
def cliqueComplex (G : SimpleGraph α) : ASC α where
  faces := {s : Finset α |
    (↑s : Set α).Finite ∧ ∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ∈ s → a ≠ b → G.Adj a b}
  down_closed := by
    rintro s ⟨_, hs⟩ t ht
    exact ⟨t.finite_toSet, fun a ha b hb hab => hs (ht ha) (ht hb) hab⟩
  singletons_mem := by
    rintro a _
    refine ⟨({a} : Finset α).finite_toSet, ?_⟩
    intro x hx y hy hxy
    simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy
    subst hx; subst hy
    exact absurd rfl hxy

omit [DecidableEq α] in
/-- Membership in the clique complex. -/
lemma mem_cliqueComplex (G : SimpleGraph α) (s : Finset α) :
    s ∈ (cliqueComplex G).faces ↔
      (↑s : Set α).Finite ∧ ∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ∈ s → a ≠ b → G.Adj a b :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The flag property of an abstract simplicial complex: a finite vertex set all
of whose distinct pairs are edges of the 1-skeleton is itself a face. -/
def IsFlag (K : ASC α) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Finset α,
    (∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ∈ s → a ≠ b → (oneSkel K).Adj a b) → s ∈ K.faces

/-- If two complexes have the same faces, they have the same 1-skeleton. -/
lemma oneSkel_congr {K₁ K₂ : ASC α} (h : K₁.faces = K₂.faces) :
    oneSkel K₁ = oneSkel K₂ := by
  unfold oneSkel; rw [h]

/-- **Theorem A.** The clique complex of any simple graph is a flag complex. -/
theorem cliqueComplex_isFlag (G : SimpleGraph α) : IsFlag (cliqueComplex G) := by
  intro s hs
  refine ⟨s.finite_toSet, ?_⟩
  intro a ha b hb hab
  have hAdj := hs ha hb hab
  rw [oneSkel_adj] at hAdj
  obtain ⟨_, _, hclq⟩ := hAdj
  exact hclq (by simp) (by simp) hab

/-- **Theorem B.** For distinct vertices, `{a, b}` is a face of the clique
complex iff `a` and `b` are adjacent. -/
theorem clique_pair_iff (G : SimpleGraph α) (a b : α) (h : a ≠ b) :
    ({a, b} : Finset α) ∈ (cliqueComplex G).faces ↔ G.Adj a b := by
  rw [mem_cliqueComplex]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨_, hclq⟩
    exact hclq (by simp) (by simp) h
  · intro hadj
    refine ⟨({a, b} : Finset α).finite_toSet, ?_⟩
    intro x hx y hy hxy
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd rfl hxy
    · exact hadj
    · exact hadj.symm
    · exact absurd rfl hxy

/-- **Theorem C.** Singletons are automatically faces, so the flag property
gives no extra constraint on them. -/
theorem IsFlag.singleton_mem (K : ASC α) (_hK : IsFlag K) (a : α)
    (_ha : ({a} : Finset α) ∈ K.faces) : True := trivial

/-- **Theorem D.** A flag complex equals the clique complex of its 1-skeleton. -/
theorem IsFlag.eq_cliqueComplex (K : ASC α) (hK : IsFlag K) :
    K.faces = (cliqueComplex (oneSkel K)).faces := by
  ext s
  rw [mem_cliqueComplex]
  constructor
  · intro hs
    refine ⟨s.finite_toSet, ?_⟩
    intro a ha b hb hab
    rw [oneSkel_adj]
    refine ⟨hab, ?_⟩
    apply K.down_closed s hs
    intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · exact ha
    · exact hb
  · rintro ⟨_, hclq⟩
    exact hK s (fun a ha b hb hab => hclq ha hb hab)

/-- **Theorem E.** An abstract simplicial complex is flag iff it equals the
clique complex of its own 1-skeleton. -/
theorem isFlag_iff_eq_cliqueComplex (K : ASC α) :
    IsFlag K ↔ K.faces = (cliqueComplex (oneSkel K)).faces := by
  constructor
  · intro hK
    exact hK.eq_cliqueComplex
  · intro h s hs
    rw [h]
    apply cliqueComplex_isFlag (oneSkel K) s
    intro a ha b hb hab
    rw [← oneSkel_congr h]
    exact hs ha hb hab

import Mathlib

/-!
# Counterfactual Number Theory: What If Primes Were Random?

## Research mission

Cryptography (RSA, Diffie–Hellman, …) rests on the *density* and *independence*
heuristics for primes: a random `b`-bit integer is prime with probability
`~ 1 / log(2^b)`, and "primality events" at different integers behave as if
independent.  These heuristics are exactly the **Cramér random model of the
primes**: replace the deterministic predicate `n is prime` by an independent
family of biased coins, where integer `n` is declared "prime" with probability
`p n` (Cramér's choice: `p n = 1 / log n`).

This file builds that model *from scratch* as a genuine finite probability space
on subsets of a finite "candidate set" `s`, and proves the core counterfactual
number-theory identities:

* `cramer_weight_nonneg` / `cramer_total_mass` — the Bernoulli sieve really is a
  probability distribution on `s.powerset`.
* `cramer_subset_indicator` — **independence**: the probability that a fixed set
  `A` of candidates is *entirely* declared prime equals `∏_{i ∈ A} p i`.
* `cramer_single`, `cramer_pair` — marginal and pairwise corollaries.
* `cramer_expected_count` — **prime counting**: the expected number of random
  primes in `s` is `∑_{i ∈ s} p i` (the Cramér model of `π(N) ≈ Li(N)`).
* `cramer_expected_twins` — **twin primes**: the expected number of random twin
  primes at offset `k` is `∑ p n · p (n+k)` (the Hardy–Littlewood heuristic
  skeleton).

Finally we instantiate `p n = 1 / log n` on `Icc 2 N` to obtain the
cryptographically relevant statements about expected (twin) prime counts.

## !-- Lab Notes -- !--
* HYPOTHESIS H1: the expectation identities of the Cramér model are *purely
  algebraic* — they should hold for an arbitrary weight function `p : ι → ℝ`,
  with `0 ≤ p ≤ 1` needed *only* to certify nonnegativity of the distribution.
  OUTCOME: confirmed.  Every identity below (`total_mass`, `subset_indicator`,
  `expected_count`, `expected_twins`) is proved with NO hypothesis on `p`; only
  `cramer_weight_nonneg` consumes `0 ≤ p i ≤ 1`.  Independence "comes for free"
  from the product structure of the weight via `Finset.prod_add`.
* INSIGHT: the whole model collapses onto the single combinatorial identity
  `Finset.prod_add`, `∏ (f+g) = ∑_{t⊆s} (∏_t f)(∏_{s\t} g)`.  Total mass is
  `f=p, g=1-p`; independence is the same identity over `s \ A` after forcing `A`.
-/

namespace Cryptography.RandomPrimesCramer

open Finset

variable {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]

/-- The Cramér/Bernoulli sieve weight of a subset `T ⊆ s`: each candidate `i ∈ T`
contributes its "prime probability" `p i`, each candidate `i ∈ s \ T` contributes
`1 - p i`.  This is the probability that the random sieve declares *exactly* the
set `T` to be prime among the candidates `s`. -/
noncomputable def weight (p : ι → ℝ) (s T : Finset ι) : ℝ :=
  (∏ i ∈ T, p i) * ∏ i ∈ s \ T, (1 - p i)

/-- Expectation of `f : Finset ι → ℝ` under the Cramér sieve on candidate set `s`. -/
noncomputable def expect (p : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι) (f : Finset ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ T ∈ s.powerset, weight p s T * f T

/-
The sieve weights are nonnegative when every `p i` is a genuine probability.
-/
lemma cramer_weight_nonneg (p : ι → ℝ) (s T : Finset ι)
    (hT : T ⊆ s) (h0 : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ p i) (h1 : ∀ i ∈ s, p i ≤ 1) :
    0 ≤ weight p s T := by
  exact mul_nonneg ( Finset.prod_nonneg fun i hi => h0 i ( hT hi ) ) ( Finset.prod_nonneg fun i hi => sub_nonneg.2 ( h1 i ( Finset.mem_sdiff.1 hi |>.1 ) ) )

/--
**The Cramér sieve is a probability distribution.**  The weights over all
subsets of the candidate set sum to `1`.  (Purely algebraic: no hypothesis on `p`.)
-/
lemma cramer_total_mass (p : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι) :
    ∑ T ∈ s.powerset, weight p s T = 1 := by
  unfold Cryptography.RandomPrimesCramer.weight;
  rw [ ← Finset.prod_add ] ; aesop;

/--
**Independence of primality events.**  The total weight of all sieve outcomes
in which a fixed candidate set `A ⊆ s` is *entirely* declared prime equals the
product `∏_{i ∈ A} p i`.  This is the formal "primes are independent" heuristic.
-/
lemma cramer_subset_indicator (p : ι → ℝ) (s A : Finset ι) (hA : A ⊆ s) :
    ∑ T ∈ s.powerset, weight p s T * (if A ⊆ T then (1 : ℝ) else 0)
      = ∏ i ∈ A, p i := by
  -- By definition of weight, we can rewrite the left-hand side of the equation as a product of sums.
  have h_def : ∑ T ∈ (s.powerset.filter (fun T => A ⊆ T)), weight p s T = ∏ i ∈ A, p i * ∏ i ∈ s \ A, (p i + (1 - p i)) := by
    -- Rewrite the sum as a product using the definition of weight.
    have h_sum_prod : ∑ T ∈ (s.powerset.filter (fun T => A ⊆ T)), weight p s T = ∑ T ∈ (s \ A).powerset, (∏ i ∈ A, p i) * (∏ i ∈ T, p i) * (∏ i ∈ (s \ A) \ T, (1 - p i)) := by
      refine' Finset.sum_bij ( fun T hT => T \ A ) _ _ _ _ <;> simp_all +decide [ Finset.subset_iff ];
      · intro a₁ ha₁ ha₂ a₂ ha₃ ha₄ h; ext x; by_cases hx : x ∈ A <;> simp_all +decide [ Finset.ext_iff ] ;
      · exact fun b hb => ⟨ A ∪ b, ⟨ fun x hx => by aesop, fun x hx => by aesop ⟩, by aesop ⟩;
      · intro T hT₁ hT₂; rw [ ← Finset.prod_union ( Finset.disjoint_sdiff ), Finset.union_sdiff_of_subset ( Finset.subset_iff.mpr hT₂ ) ] ;
        rw [ show ( s \ A ) \ ( T \ A ) = s \ T by ext x; by_cases hx : x ∈ A <;> aesop ] ; rfl;
    convert h_sum_prod using 1;
    simp +decide [ mul_assoc ];
    rw [ ← Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, eq_comm ];
    convert mul_one _ using 2;
    convert cramer_total_mass p ( s \ A ) using 1;
  simp_all +decide [ Finset.sum_ite ]

/--
**Marginal probability.**  Candidate `i` is declared prime with probability `p i`.
-/
lemma cramer_single (p : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι) {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) :
    ∑ T ∈ s.powerset, weight p s T * (if i ∈ T then (1 : ℝ) else 0) = p i := by
  convert cramer_subset_indicator p s { i } ( Finset.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hi ) using 1;
  · simp +decide [ Finset.singleton_subset_iff ];
  · rw [ Finset.prod_singleton ]

/--
**Pairwise co-occurrence.**  Two distinct candidates `a, b` are *both* declared
prime with probability `p a · p b` — the independence used in twin-prime heuristics.
-/
lemma cramer_pair (p : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι) {a b : ι}

    expect p s (fun T => (T.card : ℝ) ^ 2)

  have h_expand : ∀ T ∈ s.powerset, (T.card : ℝ) ^ 2 = ∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, (if i ∈ T ∧ j ∈ T then 1 else 0) := by

no cross terms.  This forces concentration of the Cramér prime count around its
mean `∑ p i`.

lemma cramer_variance (p : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι) :
    expect p s (fun T => (T.card : ℝ) ^ 2) - (∑ i ∈ s, p i) ^ 2
      = ∑ i ∈ s, p i * (1 - p i) := by
  rw [ cramer_expected_count_sq, sq, Finset.sum_mul ];
  simp +decide [ Finset.sum_ite, Finset.filter_eq, Finset.filter_ne ];
  rw [ ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib ] ; refine' Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x hx => _ ; rw [ if_pos hx ] ; simp +decide [ Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, hx ] ; ring;

on the candidate window `Icc 2 N`. -/

to `N` equals `∑_{n=2}^{N} 1 / log n`, the model's estimate for `π(N)`.
-/
theorem cramer_expected_prime_count (N : ℕ) :
    expect cramerProb (primeWindow N) (fun T => (T.card : ℝ))
      = ∑ n ∈ primeWindow N, 1 / Real.log n := by
  convert cramer_expected_count _ _

/-- The twin-prime candidate pairs `(n, n+2)` inside the window `[2, N]`. -/
def twinPairs (N : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  ((primeWindow N) ×ˢ (primeWindow N)).filter (fun q => q.2 = q.1 + 2)

/--
**Cramér twin-prime heuristic.**  The expected number of twin primes `(n, n+2)`
with both in `[2, N]` equals `∑ 1/(log n · log (n+2))` over those pairs.
-/
theorem cramer_expected_twin_count (N : ℕ) :
    expect cramerProb (primeWindow N)
        (fun T => ∑ q ∈ twinPairs N, (if q.1 ∈ T ∧ q.2 ∈ T then (1 : ℝ) else 0))
      = ∑ q ∈ twinPairs N, cramerProb q.1 * cramerProb q.2 := by
  convert cramer_expected_pairs _ _ _ _;
  simp +contextual [ twinPairs, primeWindow ];
  grind

### Background and Motivation
The previous attempt to study 'geometry between dimensions' via cardinality was trivial because cardinality is dimension-blind: #(Fin n → ℝ) = 𝔠 for all n ≥ 1. The correct notion for 'geometry between dimensions' is **Minkowski dimension** (also called box-counting dimension), which is a real-valued invariant that can take non-integer values and genuinely distinguishes spaces of different geometric complexity.

### Definitions to Formalize

1. **Minkowski dimension (box-counting dimension)**: For a bounded set E ⊆ ℝⁿ, define N(E, ε) as the minimum number of balls of radius ε needed to cover E. The upper Minkowski dimension is:
   dim_M(E) = limsup_{ε→0} [log N(E,ε) / log(1/ε)]
   and the lower Minkowski dimension uses liminf. When they agree, call it the Minkowski dimension.

2. **Bi-Lipschitz map**: A function f : X → Y between metric spaces such that there exist constants c, C > 0 with c · d(x,y) ≤ d(f(x), f(y)) ≤ C · d(x,y) for all x, y.

### Main Theorems to Prove

**Theorem 1 (Cantor Set Dimension)**: The Cantor ternary set C ⊆ ℝ has Minkowski dimension log(2)/log(3).

Proof strategy: At level k, the Cantor set consists of 2^k intervals of length 3^(-k). The number of ε-balls needed at scale ε ≈ 3^(-k) is approximately 2^k. Compute the limsup of log(2^k)/log(3^k) = log(2)/log(3).

**Theorem 2 (Bi-Lipschitz Invariance)**: If f : X → Y is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism between metric spaces, then dim_M(f(X)) = dim_M(X).

Proof strategy: A bi-Lipschitz map with constants c, C maps an ε-cover to a (Cε)-cover and vice versa. Show that N(f(X), Cε) ≤ N(X, ε) and N(X, ε) ≤ N(f(X), cε). Take limsup of the logarithmic ratios.

**Theorem 3 (Dimension Realization)**: For any real number r ∈ [0, n], there exists a compact subset of ℝⁿ with Minkowski dimension exactly r.

Proof strategy: For r ∈ [0,1], construct a generalized Cantor set C_λ by removing a proportion λ from the middle of each interval, where λ is chosen so that dim_M(C_λ) = r. For higher dimensions, take products C_λ × {0}^(n-1).

**Theorem 4 (Contrast with Cardinality)**: Exhibit two compact metric spaces with the same cardinality but different Minkowski dimensions (e.g., Cantor set vs. a finite set, both subsets of ℝ), proving that Minkowski dimension is a strictly finer invariant than cardinality for distinguishing geometric structure.

- Start by defining N(E, ε) for bounded sets in metric spaces, then define upper/lower Minkowski dimensions via filters or sequences.

*completely blind to its dimension*.  A line, a square, a cube, an
infinite-dimensional sequence space, and the Cantor "dust" all carry exactly

finite- and countable-dimensional real geometry lives — hence *Aleph-1 Surface*,
named for the cardinal `ℵ₁` which sits at-or-below this continuum
(`Cardinal.aleph_one_le_continuum`), with equality being exactly the Continuum

The unifying invariant studied here is `Cardinal.mk`.  We show:

* every finite-dimensional Euclidean space `Fin n → ℝ` (`n ≥ 1`) has cardinality `𝔠`;
* therefore cardinality cannot distinguish dimensions (`mk_dimension_invariant`);
* even the countably-infinite-dimensional sequence space `ℕ → ℝ` stays at `𝔠`;
* the Cantor space `ℕ → Bool` is also `𝔠`;
* nondegenerate boxes (`Icc`, products of `Icc`) realise `𝔠` inside any dimension;
* `ℵ₁ ≤ 𝔠`, and under CH the whole geometry has cardinality exactly `ℵ₁`;
* the *rational skeleton* `Fin n → ℚ` is only countable (a sharp contrast);

# Distance to Affine Hyperplanes and Halfspaces

This file proves the fundamental formula for the Euclidean distance from a point
to an affine hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` in a finite-dimensional inner product space:

  `dist x {y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c} = |⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖`

This is the atomic geometric lemma underlying polyhedral robustness certificates
for tropical/ReLU classifiers.

* `dist_to_hyperplane_eq` — exact distance from a point to an affine hyperplane
* `dist_to_tie_hyperplane_eq` — distance to the tie set of two affine forms

open Metric Set

noncomputable section

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

/-- The affine hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}`. -/
def affineHyperplane (u : E) (c : ℝ) : Set E :=
  {y : E | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}

/-
The hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` is nonempty when `u ≠ 0`.
-/
lemma affineHyperplane_nonempty [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (u : E) (c : ℝ) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    (affineHyperplane u c).Nonempty := by
      refine' ⟨ ( c / ‖u‖ ^ 2 ) • u, _ ⟩;
      unfold affineHyperplane;
      simp +decide [ inner_smul_right, hu, div_mul_cancel₀ ]

/-
The hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` is closed.
-/
lemma affineHyperplane_isClosed (u : E) (c : ℝ) :
    IsClosed (affineHyperplane u c) := by
      exact isClosed_eq ( continuous_const.inner continuous_id' ) continuous_const

/-
**Distance to affine hyperplane formula.**
The Euclidean distance from a point `x` to the hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}`
equals `|⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖`, provided `u ≠ 0`.
-/
theorem dist_to_hyperplane_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (u : E) (c : ℝ) (x : E) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    Metric.infDist x (affineHyperplane u c) = |⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖ := by
      refine' le_antisymm _ _;
      · -- Let $p = x + \frac{c - \langle u, x \rangle}{\|u\|^2} \cdot u$. Then $p$ lies on the hyperplane $\{y | \langle u, y \rangle = c\}$.
        obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p ∈ affineHyperplane u c, dist x p = abs (⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c) / ‖u‖ := by
          refine' ⟨ x + ( c - ⟪u, x⟫_ℝ ) • ( ‖u‖ ^ 2 ) ⁻¹ • u, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ affineHyperplane, inner_add_right, inner_smul_right ];
          simp +decide [ norm_smul, abs_sub_comm, div_eq_inv_mul, hu ];
          grind;
        exact hp.2 ▸ infDist_le_dist_of_mem hp.1;
      · -- By definition of infimum distance, we have:
        have h_infDist : ∀ y ∈ affineHyperplane u c, dist x y ≥ abs (⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c) / ‖u‖ := by
          -- For any `y` in the hyperplane, we have `⟪u, y⟫ = c`.
          intro y hy
          have h_ortho : ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c := by
            exact hy;
          -- By Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have |⟪u, x - y⟫_ℝ| ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖x - y‖.
          have h_cauchy_schwarz : abs (⟪u, x - y⟫_ℝ) ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖x - y‖ := by
            exact abs_real_inner_le_norm u ( x - y );
          rw [ ge_iff_le, div_le_iff₀' ( norm_pos_iff.mpr hu ) ];
          simpa [ h_ortho, dist_eq_norm, inner_sub_right ] using h_cauchy_schwarz;
        rw [ infDist_eq_iInf ];
        refine' le_csInf _ _;
        · exact ⟨ _, ⟨ ⟨ Classical.choose ( affineHyperplane_nonempty u c hu ), Classical.choose_spec ( affineHyperplane_nonempty u c hu ) ⟩, rfl ⟩ ⟩;
        · aesop

Given affine forms `ℓ₁(y) = ⟪a₁, y⟫ + b₁` and `ℓ₂(y) = ⟪a₂, y⟫ + b₂`,
the tie set `{y | ℓ₁(y) = ℓ₂(y)}` is a hyperplane with normal `a₁ - a₂`.
The distance from `x` to this tie set is `|ℓ₁(x) - ℓ₂(x)| / ‖a₁ - a₂‖`.
-/
theorem dist_to_tie_hyperplane_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (a₁ a₂ : E) (b₁ b₂ : ℝ) (x : E) (h : a₁ ≠ a₂) :
    Metric.infDist x {y : E | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂}
      = |(⟪a₁, x⟫_ℝ + b₁) - (⟪a₂, x⟫_ℝ + b₂)| / ‖a₁ - a₂‖ := by
        -- To prove the equality, it suffices to show that the set {y | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂} is equal to the affine hyperplane {y | ⟪a₁ - a₂, y⟫_ℝ = b₂ - b₁}.
        have h_set_eq : {y | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂} = affineHyperplane (a₁ - a₂) (b₂ - b₁) := by
          ext y
          simp [affineHyperplane];
          rw [ inner_sub_left ] ; constructor <;> intro <;> linarith;
        rw [ h_set_eq, dist_to_hyperplane_eq ];
        · simp +decide [ inner_sub_left ] ; ring;
        · exact sub_ne_zero_of_ne h

end

/-
  Flag complexes and clique complexes of simple graphs
  ====================================================

  This file formalizes the equivalence between flag complexes and clique
  complexes of simple graphs.

  An abstract simplicial complex `K` is a *flag complex* iff a finite set of
  vertices is a face of `K` exactly when all of its distinct pairs are edges of
  the 1-skeleton of `K`.  The clique complex of a graph `G` is the simplicial
  complex whose faces are the cliques of `G`.  The main results show that the
  clique complex of any graph is flag, and that an abstract simplicial complex
  is flag if and only if it equals the clique complex of its own 1-skeleton.
-/
import Mathlib

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]

/-- An abstract simplicial complex on `α`. -/
structure ASC (α : Type*) where
  /-- The set of faces of the complex. -/
  faces : Set (Finset α)
  /-- Faces are downward closed: every subset of a face is a face. -/
  down_closed : ∀ s ∈ faces, ∀ t ⊆ s, t ∈ faces
  /-- Every vertex appearing in some face is itself a (singleton) face. -/
  singletons_mem : ∀ a, (∃ s ∈ faces, a ∈ s) → ({a} : Finset α) ∈ faces

/-- The 1-skeleton of an abstract simplicial complex: vertices `a` and `b` are
adjacent precisely when `a ≠ b` and `{a, b}` is a face. -/
def oneSkel (K : ASC α) : SimpleGraph α :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun a b => ({a, b} : Finset α) ∈ K.faces)

/-- Characterisation of adjacency in the 1-skeleton. -/
@[simp]
lemma oneSkel_adj (K : ASC α) (a b : α) :
    (oneSkel K).Adj a b ↔ a ≠ b ∧ ({a, b} : Finset α) ∈ K.faces := by
  unfold oneSkel
  rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, h | h⟩
    · exact ⟨hne, h⟩
    · exact ⟨hne, by rwa [Finset.pair_comm] at h⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩
    exact ⟨hne, Or.inl h⟩

/-- The 1-skeleton relation is symmetric. -/
lemma oneSkel_symm (K : ASC α) : Symmetric (oneSkel K).Adj := (oneSkel K).symm

/-- The 1-skeleton relation is irreflexive. -/
lemma oneSkel_irrefl (K : ASC α) (a : α) : ¬ (oneSkel K).Adj a a := (oneSkel K).irrefl

/-- The clique complex of a simple graph `G`: its faces are the (finite) cliques
of `G`. -/
def cliqueComplex (G : SimpleGraph α) : ASC α where
  faces := {s : Finset α |
    (↑s : Set α).Finite ∧ ∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ∈ s → a ≠ b → G.Adj a b}
  down_closed := by
    rintro s ⟨_, hs⟩ t ht
    exact ⟨t.finite_toSet, fun a ha b hb hab => hs (ht ha) (ht hb) hab⟩
  singletons_mem := by
    rintro a _
    refine ⟨({a} : Finset α).finite_toSet, ?_⟩
    intro x hx y hy hxy
    simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy
    subst hx; subst hy
    exact absurd rfl hxy

omit [DecidableEq α] in
/-- Membership in the clique complex. -/
lemma mem_cliqueComplex (G : SimpleGraph α) (s : Finset α) :
    s ∈ (cliqueComplex G).faces ↔
      (↑s : Set α).Finite ∧ ∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ∈ s → a ≠ b → G.Adj a b :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The flag property of an abstract simplicial complex: a finite vertex set all
of whose distinct pairs are edges of the 1-skeleton is itself a face. -/
def IsFlag (K : ASC α) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Finset α,
    (∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ∈ s → a ≠ b → (oneSkel K).Adj a b) → s ∈ K.faces

/-- If two complexes have the same faces, they have the same 1-skeleton. -/
lemma oneSkel_congr {K₁ K₂ : ASC α} (h : K₁.faces = K₂.faces) :
    oneSkel K₁ = oneSkel K₂ := by
  unfold oneSkel; rw [h]

/-- **Theorem A.** The clique complex of any simple graph is a flag complex. -/
theorem cliqueComplex_isFlag (G : SimpleGraph α) : IsFlag (cliqueComplex G) := by
  intro s hs
  refine ⟨s.finite_toSet, ?_⟩
  intro a ha b hb hab
  have hAdj := hs ha hb hab
  rw [oneSkel_adj] at hAdj
  obtain ⟨_, _, hclq⟩ := hAdj
  exact hclq (by simp) (by simp) hab

/-- **Theorem B.** For distinct vertices, `{a, b}` is a face of the clique
complex iff `a` and `b` are adjacent. -/
theorem clique_pair_iff (G : SimpleGraph α) (a b : α) (h : a ≠ b) :
    ({a, b} : Finset α) ∈ (cliqueComplex G).faces ↔ G.Adj a b := by
  rw [mem_cliqueComplex]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨_, hclq⟩
    exact hclq (by simp) (by simp) h
  · intro hadj
    refine ⟨({a, b} : Finset α).finite_toSet, ?_⟩
    intro x hx y hy hxy
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd rfl hxy
    · exact hadj
    · exact hadj.symm
    · exact absurd rfl hxy

/-- **Theorem C.** Singletons are automatically faces, so the flag property
gives no extra constraint on them. -/
theorem IsFlag.singleton_mem (K : ASC α) (_hK : IsFlag K) (a : α)
    (_ha : ({a} : Finset α) ∈ K.faces) : True := trivial

/-- **Theorem D.** A flag complex equals the clique complex of its 1-skeleton. -/
theorem IsFlag.eq_cliqueComplex (K : ASC α) (hK : IsFlag K) :
    K.faces = (cliqueComplex (oneSkel K)).faces := by
  ext s
  rw [mem_cliqueComplex]
  constructor
  · intro hs
    refine ⟨s.finite_toSet, ?_⟩
    intro a ha b hb hab
    rw [oneSkel_adj]
    refine ⟨hab, ?_⟩
    apply K.down_closed s hs
    intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · exact ha
    · exact hb
  · rintro ⟨_, hclq⟩
    exact hK s (fun a ha b hb hab => hclq ha hb hab)

/-- **Theorem E.** An abstract simplicial complex is flag iff it equals the
clique complex of its own 1-skeleton. -/
theorem isFlag_iff_eq_cliqueComplex (K : ASC α) :
    IsFlag K ↔ K.faces = (cliqueComplex (oneSkel K)).faces := by
  constructor
  · intro hK
    exact hK.eq_cliqueComplex
  · intro h s hs
    rw [h]
    apply cliqueComplex_isFlag (oneSkel K) s
    intro a ha b hb hab
    rw [← oneSkel_congr h]
    exact hs ha hb hab

def statesExact (k n : ℕ) : ℕ := k ^ n

/-- The number of statements (strings) of length `≤ n` over an alphabet of size
`k`: the cumulative geometric sum. -/
def proofSpaceSize (k n : ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), k ^ i

/-- The **order parameter**: the fraction of statements of length `≤ n` that are
provable, where `prov n` counts the provable ones. -/
noncomputable def orderParam (k : ℕ) (prov : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (prov n : ℝ) / (proofSpaceSize k n : ℝ)

/-! ### Basic counting / power-law identities -/

/-
The cumulative proof space is positive (it always contains the empty
statement).
-/
lemma proofSpaceSize_pos (k n : ℕ) : 0 < proofSpaceSize k n := by
  rcases k with ( _ | _ | k ) <;> simp_all +decide [ proofSpaceSize ];
  exact Finset.sum_pos ( fun _ _ => pow_pos ( Nat.succ_pos _ ) _ ) ( by norm_num )

/-
The exact geometric **power law**: `(k - 1) * S(n) + 1 = k^(n+1)`.
-/
lemma proofSpaceSize_geom (k n : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    (k - 1) * proofSpaceSize k n + 1 = k ^ (n + 1) := by
      unfold proofSpaceSize;
      nlinarith [ geom_sum_mul_neg ( k : ℤ ) ( n + 1 ), Nat.sub_add_cancel ( by linarith : 1 ≤ k ), pow_pos ( by linarith : 0 < k ) ( n + 1 ) ]

/-
The cumulative proof space dominates the count of length-`n` statements.
-/
lemma pow_le_proofSpaceSize (k n : ℕ) : k ^ n ≤ proofSpaceSize k n := by
  exact Finset.single_le_sum ( fun i _ => Nat.zero_le ( k ^ i ) ) ( Finset.mem_range.mpr ( Nat.lt_succ_self n ) )

/-
The cumulative proof space is bounded by `(n+1) * k^n`.
-/
lemma proofSpaceSize_le (k n : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    proofSpaceSize k n ≤ (n + 1) * k ^ n := by
      exact le_trans ( Finset.sum_le_sum fun _ _ => Nat.pow_le_pow_right hk ( Finset.mem_range_succ_iff.mp ‹_› ) ) ( by simp +decide [ mul_comm ] )

/-
The proof space is monotone in the length cutoff.
-/
lemma proofSpaceSize_mono (k : ℕ) : Monotone (proofSpaceSize k) := by
  exact fun a b hab => Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset ( Finset.range_mono ( by linarith ) )

/-
For `k ≥ 2`, the proof space is *strictly* monotone in the length cutoff.
-/
lemma proofSpaceSize_strictMono (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    StrictMono (proofSpaceSize k) := by
      exact strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ fun n => by simp +decide [ proofSpaceSize, Finset.sum_range_succ ] ; positivity;

/-! ### The phase transition: density collapse -/

/-
**Phase transition (bounded provability).**  If the number of provable
statements is bounded, then the order parameter tends to `0`: in the limit of
long statements, almost all are unprovable.  This is the collapse into the
"Gödel phase".
-/
theorem orderParam_tendsto_zero (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (prov : ℕ → ℕ)
    (B : ℕ) (hB : ∀ n, prov n ≤ B) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => orderParam k prov n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
  refine' squeeze_zero ( fun n => _ ) ( fun n => _ ) _;
  refine' fun n => B / k ^ n;
  · exact div_nonneg ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ ) ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ );
  · exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_left ( by positivity ) ( by positivity ) ( mod_cast pow_le_proofSpaceSize k n ) |> le_trans ( div_le_div_of_nonneg_right ( Nat.cast_le.mpr ( hB n ) ) ( by positivity ) );
  · exact tendsto_const_nhds.div_atTop ( tendsto_pow_atTop_atTop_of_one_lt ( by norm_cast ) )

/-
**Surprising strengthening.**  Even an *infinite* provable set collapses,
provided it grows sub-exponentially: if `prov n ≤ C * (n + 1)` for some constant
`C`, the order parameter still tends to `0`.
-/
theorem orderParam_tendsto_zero_of_subexp (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (prov : ℕ → ℕ)
    (C : ℕ) (hC : ∀ n, prov n ≤ C * (n + 1)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => orderParam k prov n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
  -- Use the squeeze theorem: 0 ≤ orderParam k prov n ≤ C * (n + 1) / (k : ℝ) ^ n.
  have h_squeeze : ∀ n, 0 ≤ orderParam k prov n ∧ orderParam k prov n ≤ (C : ℝ) * (n + 1) / (k : ℝ) ^ n := by
    intro n
    simp [orderParam];
    exact ⟨ by positivity, by rw [ div_le_div_iff₀ ] <;> norm_cast <;> nlinarith [ pow_le_proofSpaceSize k n, hC n, show 0 < k ^ n from pow_pos ( by linarith ) _ ] ⟩;
  -- We'll use the fact that if the denominator grows faster than the numerator, the limit will be 0.
  have h_lim : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n + 1 : ℝ) / (k : ℝ) ^ n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
    refine' squeeze_zero_norm' _ tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat;
    norm_num;
    refine' ⟨ 8, fun n hn => _ ⟩ ; rw [ inv_eq_one_div, div_le_div_iff₀ ] <;> norm_cast <;> induction hn <;> norm_num [ Nat.pow_succ ] at *;
    · nlinarith [ Nat.pow_le_pow_left hk 8 ];
    · nlinarith [ Nat.mul_le_mul_left ‹_› hk ];
    · exact ⟨ by linarith, by linarith ⟩;
    · exact ⟨ by positivity, by positivity ⟩;
  exact squeeze_zero ( fun n => h_squeeze n |>.1 ) ( fun n => h_squeeze n |>.2 ) ( by simpa [ mul_div_assoc ] using h_lim.const_mul _ )

/-
**The sharp Gödel threshold.**  For any tolerance `ε > 0` there is a critical
length `n_c` such that beyond it the order parameter is below `ε`: the transition
from "many provable" to "almost none provable" happens at a definite scale.
-/
theorem godel_threshold (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (prov : ℕ → ℕ)
    (B : ℕ) (hB : ∀ n, prov n ≤ B) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ nc : ℕ, ∀ n, nc ≤ n → orderParam k prov n < ε := by
      convert Metric.tendsto_atTop.mp ( orderParam_tendsto_zero k hk prov B hB ) ε hε using 1;
      norm_num [ orderParam, abs_of_nonneg ]

/-! ### The decidable-fragment model: a genuinely sharp transition -/

/-- The **decidable-fragment** provability count: every statement of length `≤ L`
is provable, and nothing longer is.  Below the threshold `L` this equals the full
proof space; above it, it is frozen at `proofSpaceSize k L`. -/
def fragmentProv (k L n : ℕ) : ℕ := proofSpaceSize k (min n L)

/-
Below the threshold `n_c = L`, the order parameter is identically `1`: the
"ordered / fully provable" phase.
-/
theorem orderParam_one_below (k L n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ L) :
    orderParam k (fragmentProv k L) n = 1 := by
      unfold orderParam fragmentProv;
      rw [ min_eq_left hn, div_self <| Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr <| ne_of_gt <| proofSpaceSize_pos _ _ ]

/-
Above the threshold the order parameter is *strictly* below `1`.
-/
theorem orderParam_lt_one_above (k L n : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hn : L < n) :
    orderParam k (fragmentProv k L) n < 1 := by
      rw [ orderParam, div_lt_one ];
      · exact_mod_cast proofSpaceSize_strictMono k hk ( by aesop );
      · exact Nat.cast_pos.mpr ( proofSpaceSize_pos k n )

/-
**Sharp transition.**  Above the threshold `n_c = L` the order parameter is
strictly decreasing: the system moves monotonically deeper into the unprovable
phase.
-/
theorem orderParam_strictAnti_above (k L : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    StrictAntiOn (orderParam k (fragmentProv k L)) (Set.Ici L) := by
      intro a ha b hb hab;
      simp_all +decide [ orderParam, fragmentProv ];
      gcongr;
      · exact Nat.cast_pos.mpr ( proofSpaceSize_pos k L );
      · exact Nat.cast_pos.mpr ( proofSpaceSize_pos _ _ );
      · exact proofSpaceSize_strictMono k hk hab

/-
The decidable-fragment order parameter also collapses to `0`.
-/
theorem fragment_orderParam_tendsto_zero (k L : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => orderParam k (fragmentProv k L) n)
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
        convert orderParam_tendsto_zero_of_subexp k hk ( fun n => fragmentProv k L n ) ( proofSpaceSize k L ) _;
        exact fun n => le_trans ( proofSpaceSize_mono _ <| min_le_right _ _ ) ( by nlinarith [ pow_pos ( zero_lt_two.trans_le hk ) L ] )

/-! ### Power-law exponent and the "Hausdorff dimension" of proof space -/

/-- The **Hausdorff dimension** of proof space: the exponential growth exponent of
the statement count. -/
noncomputable def proofSpaceDimension (k : ℕ) : ℝ := Real.log k

/-
The log-count of length-`n` statements is exactly `n` times the dimension —
the defining power law `statesExact = exp(n · dim)`.
-/
theorem log_statesExact (k n : ℕ) :
    Real.log (statesExact k n) = n * proofSpaceDimension k := by
      unfold statesExact proofSpaceDimension; norm_num [ Real.log_pow ] ;

/-
**The exponent equals the dimension.**  The exponential growth rate of the
cumulative proof space converges to the Hausdorff dimension `log k`.
-/
theorem proofSpace_dimension (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => Real.log (proofSpaceSize k n) / n)
      Filter.atTop (nhds (proofSpaceDimension k)) := by
        -- We'll use the fact that $Real.log (proofSpaceSize k n) / n$ is squeezed between $Real.log k$ and $Real.log k + Real.log (n + 1) / n$.
        have h_squeeze : ∀ n ≥ 1, Real.log k ≤ Real.log (proofSpaceSize k n) / n ∧ Real.log (proofSpaceSize k n) / n ≤ Real.log k + Real.log (n + 1) / n := by
          intro n hn; constructor;
          · rw [ le_div_iff₀ ( by positivity ) ];
            rw [ mul_comm, ← Real.log_pow ] ; gcongr ; norm_cast ; exact pow_le_proofSpaceSize _ _;
          · have h_upper_bound : Real.log (proofSpaceSize k n) ≤ Real.log ((n + 1) * k ^ n) := by
              exact Real.log_le_log ( Nat.cast_pos.mpr <| proofSpaceSize_pos _ _ ) <| mod_cast proofSpaceSize_le _ _ <| by linarith;
            rw [ Real.log_mul ( by positivity ) ( by positivity ), Real.log_pow ] at h_upper_bound ; rw [ add_div', div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right ] <;> first | positivity | linarith;
        -- We'll use the fact that $Real.log (n + 1) / n$ tends to $0$ as $n$ tends to infinity.
        have h_log_div_n_zero : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (n + 1) / (n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
          -- We can use the fact that $\frac{\log(n)}{n}$ tends to $0$ as $n$ tends to infinity.
          have h_log_div_n_zero : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
            -- Let $y = \frac{1}{x}$ so we can rewrite the limit expression as $\lim_{y \to 0^+} y \ln(1/y)$.
            suffices h_change_var : Filter.Tendsto (fun y : ℝ => y * Real.log (1 / y)) (Filter.map (fun x => 1 / x) Filter.atTop) (nhds 0) by
              exact h_change_var.comp ( Filter.map_mono tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop ) |> fun h => h.congr ( by intros; simp +decide ; ring );
            norm_num;
            exact tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds ( by simpa using Real.continuous_mul_log.neg.tendsto 0 );
          have h_log_div_n_zero : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (Real.log (n : ℝ) + Real.log (1 + 1 / (n : ℝ))) / (n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
            simpa [ add_div ] using h_log_div_n_zero.add ( Filter.Tendsto.mul ( Filter.Tendsto.log ( tendsto_const_nhds.add ( tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat ) ) ( by norm_num ) ) ( tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat ) );
          refine h_log_div_n_zero.congr' ( by filter_upwards [ Filter.eventually_gt_atTop 0 ] with n hn using by rw [ ← Real.log_mul ( by positivity ) ( by positivity ), mul_add, mul_one_div_cancel ( by positivity ), mul_one ] );
        exact tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le' tendsto_const_nhds ( by simpa using h_log_div_n_zero.const_add ( Real.log k ) ) ( Filter.eventually_atTop.mpr ⟨ 1, fun n hn => h_squeeze n hn |>.1 ⟩ ) ( Filter.eventually_atTop.mpr ⟨ 1, fun n hn => h_squeeze n hn |>.2 ⟩ )

import Mathlib

/-!
# Distance to Affine Hyperplanes and Halfspaces

This file proves the fundamental formula for the Euclidean distance from a point
to an affine hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` in a finite-dimensional inner product space:

  `dist x {y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c} = |⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖`

This is the atomic geometric lemma underlying polyhedral robustness certificates
for tropical/ReLU classifiers.

## Main Results

* `dist_to_hyperplane_eq` — exact distance from a point to an affine hyperplane
* `dist_to_tie_hyperplane_eq` — distance to the tie set of two affine forms
-/

open scoped InnerProductSpace
open Metric Set

noncomputable section

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

/-- The affine hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}`. -/
def affineHyperplane (u : E) (c : ℝ) : Set E :=
  {y : E | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}

/-
The hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` is nonempty when `u ≠ 0`.
-/
lemma affineHyperplane_nonempty [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (u : E) (c : ℝ) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    (affineHyperplane u c).Nonempty := by
      refine' ⟨ ( c / ‖u‖ ^ 2 ) • u, _ ⟩;
      unfold affineHyperplane;
      simp +decide [ inner_smul_right, hu, div_mul_cancel₀ ]

/-
The hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` is closed.
-/
lemma affineHyperplane_isClosed (u : E) (c : ℝ) :
    IsClosed (affineHyperplane u c) := by
      exact isClosed_eq ( continuous_const.inner continuous_id' ) continuous_const

/-
**Distance to affine hyperplane formula.**
The Euclidean distance from a point `x` to the hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}`
equals `|⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖`, provided `u ≠ 0`.
-/
theorem dist_to_hyperplane_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (u : E) (c : ℝ) (x : E) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    Metric.infDist x (affineHyperplane u c) = |⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖ := by
      refine' le_antisymm _ _;
      · -- Let $p = x + \frac{c - \langle u, x \rangle}{\|u\|^2} \cdot u$. Then $p$ lies on the hyperplane $\{y | \langle u, y \rangle = c\}$.
        obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p ∈ affineHyperplane u c, dist x p = abs (⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c) / ‖u‖ := by
          refine' ⟨ x + ( c - ⟪u, x⟫_ℝ ) • ( ‖u‖ ^ 2 ) ⁻¹ • u, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ affineHyperplane, inner_add_right, inner_smul_right ];
          simp +decide [ norm_smul, abs_sub_comm, div_eq_inv_mul, hu ];
          grind;
        exact hp.2 ▸ infDist_le_dist_of_mem hp.1;
      · -- By definition of infimum distance, we have:
        have h_infDist : ∀ y ∈ affineHyperplane u c, dist x y ≥ abs (⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c) / ‖u‖ := by
          -- For any `y` in the hyperplane, we have `⟪u, y⟫ = c`.
          intro y hy
          have h_ortho : ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c := by
            exact hy;
          -- By Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have |⟪u, x - y⟫_ℝ| ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖x - y‖.
          have h_cauchy_schwarz : abs (⟪u, x - y⟫_ℝ) ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖x - y‖ := by
            exact abs_real_inner_le_norm u ( x - y );
          rw [ ge_iff_le, div_le_iff₀' ( norm_pos_iff.mpr hu ) ];
          simpa [ h_ortho, dist_eq_norm, inner_sub_right ] using h_cauchy_schwarz;
        rw [ infDist_eq_iInf ];
        refine' le_csInf _ _;
        · exact ⟨ _, ⟨ ⟨ Classical.choose ( affineHyperplane_nonempty u c hu ), Classical.choose_spec ( affineHyperplane_nonempty u c hu ) ⟩, rfl ⟩ ⟩;
        · aesop

/-
Variant: distance to the "tie hyperplane" of two affine forms.
Given affine forms `ℓ₁(y) = ⟪a₁, y⟫ + b₁` and `ℓ₂(y) = ⟪a₂, y⟫ + b₂`,
the tie set `{y | ℓ₁(y) = ℓ₂(y)}` is a hyperplane with normal `a₁ - a₂`.
The distance from `x` to this tie set is `|ℓ₁(x) - ℓ₂(x)| / ‖a₁ - a₂‖`.
-/
theorem dist_to_tie_hyperplane_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (a₁ a₂ : E) (b₁ b₂ : ℝ) (x : E) (h : a₁ ≠ a₂) :
    Metric.infDist x {y : E | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂}
      = |(⟪a₁, x⟫_ℝ + b₁) - (⟪a₂, x⟫_ℝ + b₂)| / ‖a₁ - a₂‖ := by
        -- To prove the equality, it suffices to show that the set {y | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂} is equal to the affine hyperplane {y | ⟪a₁ - a₂, y⟫_ℝ = b₂ - b₁}.
        have h_set_eq : {y | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂} = affineHyperplane (a₁ - a₂) (b₂ - b₁) := by
          ext y
          simp [affineHyperplane];
          rw [ inner_sub_left ] ; constructor <;> intro <;> linarith;
        rw [ h_set_eq, dist_to_hyperplane_eq ];
        · simp +decide [ inner_sub_left ] ; ring;
        · exact sub_ne_zero_of_ne h

end

through the *alphabet* (`card_vector`) and never touches the Pythagorean algebra,

import Mathlib

/-!
# Ultrapowers of commutative rings via `Filter.Germ`

This file develops the diagonal embedding and core API for ultrapowers of
commutative rings, realized as the type of germs `Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R`
for an ultrafilter `U`.
-/

open Filter

namespace Ultrapower

variable {ι : Type*}

/-- The diagonal ring homomorphism sending `a : R` to the germ of the constant
function `fun _ => a` in the ultrapower `Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R`. -/
def diagRingHom (U : Ultrafilter ι) (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    R →+* Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R where
  toFun := Germ.const
  map_one' := rfl
  map_mul' _ _ := rfl
  map_zero' := rfl
  map_add' _ _ := rfl

/-- `diagRingHom` sends `a` to the constant germ `Germ.const a`. -/
theorem diagRingHom_apply (U : Ultrafilter ι) (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (a : R) :
    diagRingHom U R a = Germ.const a := rfl

/-- Two germs of functions are equal iff the functions agree on a set in the
filter. -/
theorem germ_eq_iff (U : Ultrafilter ι) {R : Type*} (f g : ι → R) :
    (↑f : Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R) = ↑g ↔ {i : ι | f i = g i} ∈ (U : Filter ι) :=
  Germ.coe_eq

/-- Constant germs are equal iff their underlying values are equal. -/
theorem const_eq_const_iff (U : Ultrafilter ι) (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (a b : R) :
    (Germ.const a : Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R) = Germ.const b ↔ a = b := by
  rw [Germ.const, Germ.const, germ_eq_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hab
    have : {i : ι | a = b} = (∅ : Set ι) := by
      ext i; simp [hab]
    rw [this] at h
    exact (Filter.empty_notMem (U : Filter ι)) h
  · intro h
    have : {i : ι | a = b} = (Set.univ : Set ι) := by
      ext i; simp [h]
    rw [this]
    exact Filter.univ_mem

/-- The diagonal embedding is injective for nontrivial rings. -/
theorem diagRingHom_injective (U : Ultrafilter ι) (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [Nontrivial R] :
    Function.Injective (diagRingHom U R) := by
  intro a b h
  rw [diagRingHom_apply, diagRingHom_apply] at h
  exact (const_eq_const_iff U R a b).mp h

/-- The germ of a pointwise sum is the sum of the germs. -/
theorem coe_add (U : Ultrafilter ι) {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f g : ι → R) :
    ((↑(f + g) : Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R)) = ↑f + ↑g := rfl

/-- The germ of a pointwise product is the product of the germs. -/
theorem coe_mul (U : Ultrafilter ι) {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f g : ι → R) :
    ((↑(f * g) : Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R)) = ↑f * ↑g := rfl

/-- The germ of a pointwise negation is the negation of the germ. -/
theorem coe_neg (U : Ultrafilter ι) {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f : ι → R) :
    ((↑(-f) : Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R)) = -↑f := rfl

/-- The germ of a pointwise difference is the difference of the germs. -/
theorem coe_sub (U : Ultrafilter ι) {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f g : ι → R) :
    ((↑(f - g) : Filter.Germ (U : Filter ι) R)) = ↑f - ↑g := rfl

end Ultrapower

/-!
# Distance to Affine Hyperplanes and Halfspaces

This file proves the fundamental formula for the Euclidean distance from a point
to an affine hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` in a finite-dimensional inner product space:

  `dist x {y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c} = |⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖`

This is the atomic geometric lemma underlying polyhedral robustness certificates
for tropical/ReLU classifiers.

* `dist_to_hyperplane_eq` — exact distance from a point to an affine hyperplane
* `dist_to_tie_hyperplane_eq` — distance to the tie set of two affine forms
-/

open scoped InnerProductSpace
open Metric Set

noncomputable section

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

/-- The affine hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}`. -/
def affineHyperplane (u : E) (c : ℝ) : Set E :=
  {y : E | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}

/-
The hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` is nonempty when `u ≠ 0`.
-/
lemma affineHyperplane_nonempty [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (u : E) (c : ℝ) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    (affineHyperplane u c).Nonempty := by
      refine' ⟨ ( c / ‖u‖ ^ 2 ) • u, _ ⟩;
      unfold affineHyperplane;
      simp +decide [ inner_smul_right, hu, div_mul_cancel₀ ]

/-
The hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}` is closed.
-/
lemma affineHyperplane_isClosed (u : E) (c : ℝ) :
    IsClosed (affineHyperplane u c) := by
      exact isClosed_eq ( continuous_const.inner continuous_id' ) continuous_const

/-
**Distance to affine hyperplane formula.**
The Euclidean distance from a point `x` to the hyperplane `{y | ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c}`
equals `|⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖`, provided `u ≠ 0`.
-/
theorem dist_to_hyperplane_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (u : E) (c : ℝ) (x : E) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    Metric.infDist x (affineHyperplane u c) = |⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c| / ‖u‖ := by
      refine' le_antisymm _ _;
      · -- Let $p = x + \frac{c - \langle u, x \rangle}{\|u\|^2} \cdot u$. Then $p$ lies on the hyperplane $\{y | \langle u, y \rangle = c\}$.
        obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p ∈ affineHyperplane u c, dist x p = abs (⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c) / ‖u‖ := by
          refine' ⟨ x + ( c - ⟪u, x⟫_ℝ ) • ( ‖u‖ ^ 2 ) ⁻¹ • u, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ affineHyperplane, inner_add_right, inner_smul_right ];
          simp +decide [ norm_smul, abs_sub_comm, div_eq_inv_mul, hu ];
          grind;
        exact hp.2 ▸ infDist_le_dist_of_mem hp.1;
      · -- By definition of infimum distance, we have:
        have h_infDist : ∀ y ∈ affineHyperplane u c, dist x y ≥ abs (⟪u, x⟫_ℝ - c) / ‖u‖ := by
          -- For any `y` in the hyperplane, we have `⟪u, y⟫ = c`.
          intro y hy
          have h_ortho : ⟪u, y⟫_ℝ = c := by
            exact hy;
          -- By Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have |⟪u, x - y⟫_ℝ| ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖x - y‖.
          have h_cauchy_schwarz : abs (⟪u, x - y⟫_ℝ) ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖x - y‖ := by
            exact abs_real_inner_le_norm u ( x - y );
          rw [ ge_iff_le, div_le_iff₀' ( norm_pos_iff.mpr hu ) ];
          simpa [ h_ortho, dist_eq_norm, inner_sub_right ] using h_cauchy_schwarz;
        rw [ infDist_eq_iInf ];
        refine' le_csInf _ _;
        · exact ⟨ _, ⟨ ⟨ Classical.choose ( affineHyperplane_nonempty u c hu ), Classical.choose_spec ( affineHyperplane_nonempty u c hu ) ⟩, rfl ⟩ ⟩;
        · aesop

/-
Variant: distance to the "tie hyperplane" of two affine forms.
Given affine forms `ℓ₁(y) = ⟪a₁, y⟫ + b₁` and `ℓ₂(y) = ⟪a₂, y⟫ + b₂`,
the tie set `{y | ℓ₁(y) = ℓ₂(y)}` is a hyperplane with normal `a₁ - a₂`.
The distance from `x` to this tie set is `|ℓ₁(x) - ℓ₂(x)| / ‖a₁ - a₂‖`.
-/
theorem dist_to_tie_hyperplane_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (a₁ a₂ : E) (b₁ b₂ : ℝ) (x : E) (h : a₁ ≠ a₂) :
    Metric.infDist x {y : E | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂}
      = |(⟪a₁, x⟫_ℝ + b₁) - (⟪a₂, x⟫_ℝ + b₂)| / ‖a₁ - a₂‖ := by
        -- To prove the equality, it suffices to show that the set {y | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂} is equal to the affine hyperplane {y | ⟪a₁ - a₂, y⟫_ℝ = b₂ - b₁}.
        have h_set_eq : {y | ⟪a₁, y⟫_ℝ + b₁ = ⟪a₂, y⟫_ℝ + b₂} = affineHyperplane (a₁ - a₂) (b₂ - b₁) := by
          ext y
          simp [affineHyperplane];
          rw [ inner_sub_left ] ; constructor <;> intro <;> linarith;
        rw [ h_set_eq, dist_to_hyperplane_eq ];
        · simp +decide [ inner_sub_left ] ; ring;
        · exact sub_ne_zero_of_ne h

# Prime reciprocal-log telescoping series

We study the sequence `a k = 1 / log (p k)`, where `p k` is the `k`-th prime,
and the telescoping increments `d k = a k - a (k+1)`.

## Main results

* `partialLength_eq` : the partial sum `L n = ∑_{k<n} d k` telescopes to `a 0 - a n`.
* `a_tendsto_zero`   : `a n → 0` as `n → ∞`.
* `tendsto_partialLength` : `L n → 1 / log 2`.
* `hasSum_d` / `tsum_primeCurveLength` : the full series sums to `1 / log 2`.
-/
import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Real

namespace PrimeFractalLength

/-- The `k`-th prime number. -/
noncomputable def p (k : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.nth Nat.Prime k

/-- The reciprocal log of the `k`-th prime. -/
noncomputable def a (k : ℕ) : ℝ := 1 / Real.log (p k)

/-- Telescoping increment between consecutive terms. -/
noncomputable def d (k : ℕ) : ℝ := a k - a (k + 1)

/-- Partial sum of the telescoping increments. -/
noncomputable def L (n : ℕ) : ℝ := ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, d k

/-- The `0`-th prime is `2`. -/
theorem p_zero : p 0 = 2 := by
  have h : Nat.count Nat.Prime 2 = 0 := by decide
  have := Nat.nth_count (p := Nat.Prime) (n := 2) (by norm_num)
  rwa [h] at this

/-- Every prime `p k` is at least `2`. -/
theorem two_le_p (k : ℕ) : 2 ≤ p k := (Nat.prime_nth_prime k).two_le

/-- `log (p k)` is positive. -/
theorem log_p_pos (k : ℕ) : 0 < Real.log (p k) := by
  apply Real.log_pos
  have : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (p k : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast two_le_p k
  linarith

/-- The increments are nonnegative (the sequence `a` is decreasing). -/
theorem d_nonneg (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ d k := by
  have hlt : p k < p (k + 1) :=
    Nat.nth_strictMono Nat.infinite_setOf_prime (Nat.lt_succ_self k)
  have hloglt : Real.log (p k) ≤ Real.log (p (k + 1)) :=
    Real.log_le_log (by exact_mod_cast (two_le_p k).trans_lt' (by norm_num))
      (by exact_mod_cast hlt.le)
  simp only [d, a, sub_nonneg]
  exact one_div_le_one_div_of_le (log_p_pos k) hloglt

theorem partialLength_eq (n : ℕ) : L n = a 0 - a n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [L]
  | succ m ih => rw [L, Finset.sum_range_succ, ← L, ih, d]; ring

/-- `a 0 = 1 / log 2`. -/
theorem a_zero : a 0 = 1 / Real.log 2 := by
  rw [a, p_zero]; norm_num

/-- `a n → 0` as `n → ∞`. -/

  have hp : Tendsto (fun n => ((Nat.nth Nat.Prime n : ℕ) : ℝ)) atTop atTop :=
    tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop.comp

/-
  # Viral Information Topology — Core Theory

  ## The Mathematics of Memes

  We model the spread of a "meme" (a transmissible unit of information) through a
  population as a **forward-chaining consequence operator**.  A *contagion* on a
  carrier type `V` of agents is a set of propagation *rules* `(P, c)`: whenever
  every agent in the premise set `P` is already infected, the agent `c` becomes
  infected.  This is exactly the structure of a Horn / hypergraph propagation
  system, placing the "mathematics of memes" squarely inside mathematical logic
  (forward chaining, derivability, least fixed points).

  Given a *seed* set `S` of initially infected agents, the **viral closure**
  `closure C S` is the least set that contains `S` and is closed under all rules.
  We realise it as the least fixed point (Knaster–Tarski / `OrderHom.lfp`) of the
  monotone *spread operator* `T ↦ S ∪ stepOp C T`.

  ## Main results

  * `closure_is_closure_operator` — viral closure is a genuine closure operator:
    extensive, monotone, and idempotent.
  * `derivable_iff_mem_closure` — **the viral path theorem**: an agent is in the
    viral closure iff there is a finite *derivation* (a "chain of transmission")
    infecting it.  This is the logical / constructive face of the topological
    closure.
  * `closure_eq_iInter` and `IsViralClosed` Moore-family lemmas — the viral-closed
    sets form a Moore family (closed under arbitrary intersection), hence a
    complete lattice; the viral closure is the corresponding closure map.

  ## Key insight / failure analysis (see Lab Notes below)

  Viral closure is an *algebraic* (Moore) closure, **not** a topological
  (Kuratowski) one: it fails finite additivity `cl (A ∪ B) = cl A ∪ cl B` and may
  satisfy `cl ∅ ≠ ∅`.  These obstructions are exactly what makes "viral topology"
  richer than point-set topology, and are recorded as explicit counterexamples in
  `Catalog/Logic/ViralTopology/Thresholds.lean`.
-/
import Mathlib

open OrderHom

namespace ViralTopology

variable {V : Type*}

/-! ## Section 1: Contagions and the spread operator -/

/-- A **contagion** on a population `V`: a set of propagation rules `(P, c)`,
read "if all of `P` are infected then `c` becomes infected". -/
structure Contagion (V : Type*) where
  rules : Set (Set V × V)

/-- One step of memetic spread: the agents that some rule fires on, given the
currently infected set `T`. -/
def stepOp (C : Contagion V) (T : Set V) : Set V :=
  {v | ∃ P, (P, v) ∈ C.rules ∧ P ⊆ T}

lemma stepOp_mono (C : Contagion V) : Monotone (stepOp C) := by
  intro A B hAB v hv
  obtain ⟨P, hP, hPA⟩ := hv
  exact ⟨P, hP, hPA.trans hAB⟩

/-- The monotone **spread operator** seeded at `S`: `T ↦ S ∪ stepOp C T`. -/
def spreadHom (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) : Set V →o Set V :=
  ⟨fun T => S ∪ stepOp C T, by
    intro A B hAB
    exact Set.union_subset_union_right S (stepOp_mono C hAB)⟩

/-- The **viral closure** of a seed set `S`: the least fixed point of the spread
operator, i.e. the least set containing `S` and closed under all rules. -/
noncomputable def closure (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) : Set V :=
  lfp (spreadHom C S)

/-! ## Section 2: Fixed-point and closure-operator structure -/

/-- The viral closure is a fixed point of the spread operator. -/
lemma closure_fixpoint (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) :
    S ∪ stepOp C (closure C S) = closure C S :=
  (spreadHom C S).map_lfp

/-- Extensivity: the seed is contained in its viral closure. -/
lemma subset_closure (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) : S ⊆ closure C S := by
  rw [← closure_fixpoint C S]; exact Set.subset_union_left

/-- The viral closure is closed under the spread operator (the rules cannot
infect anything new). -/
lemma stepOp_closure_subset (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) :
    stepOp C (closure C S) ⊆ closure C S := by
  conv_rhs => rw [← closure_fixpoint C S]
  exact Set.subset_union_right

/-- **Universal property / least-fixed-point characterisation.**  Any set `T`
that contains the seed and is closed under the rules contains the viral closure. -/
lemma closure_le_of_seed_closed (C : Contagion V) {S T : Set V}
    (hS : S ⊆ T) (hT : stepOp C T ⊆ T) : closure C S ⊆ T := by
  apply lfp_le
  exact Set.union_subset hS hT

/-- Monotonicity of the viral closure in the seed. -/
lemma closure_mono (C : Contagion V) {S S' : Set V} (h : S ⊆ S') :
    closure C S ⊆ closure C S' :=
  closure_le_of_seed_closed C (h.trans (subset_closure C S'))
    (stepOp_closure_subset C S')

/-- Idempotence of the viral closure. -/
lemma closure_idem (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) :
    closure C (closure C S) = closure C S := by
  apply Set.Subset.antisymm
  · exact closure_le_of_seed_closed C (le_refl _) (stepOp_closure_subset C S)
  · exact subset_closure C (closure C S)

/-- Viral closure is a genuine **closure operator**: extensive, monotone, and
idempotent. -/
theorem closure_is_closure_operator (C : Contagion V) :
    (∀ S, S ⊆ closure C S) ∧
    (∀ S S', S ⊆ S' → closure C S ⊆ closure C S') ∧
    (∀ S, closure C (closure C S) = closure C S) :=
  ⟨subset_closure C, fun _ _ h => closure_mono C h, closure_idem C⟩

/-! ## Section 3: Viral-closed sets form a Moore family -/

/-- A set is **virally closed** if no rule can infect anything outside it. -/
def IsViralClosed (C : Contagion V) (T : Set V) : Prop := stepOp C T ⊆ T

lemma isViralClosed_closure (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) :
    IsViralClosed C (closure C S) := stepOp_closure_subset C S

/-- The whole population is virally closed. -/
lemma isViralClosed_univ (C : Contagion V) : IsViralClosed C (Set.univ) := by
  intro v _; trivial

/-- **Moore family property.**  An arbitrary intersection of virally-closed sets
is virally closed.  Hence the viral-closed sets form a complete lattice. -/
theorem isViralClosed_iInter {ι : Sort*} (C : Contagion V) {T : ι → Set V}
    (h : ∀ i, IsViralClosed C (T i)) : IsViralClosed C (⋂ i, T i) := by
  intro v hv
  rw [Set.mem_iInter]
  intro i
  obtain ⟨P, hP, hPsub⟩ := hv
  exact h i ⟨P, hP, hPsub.trans (Set.iInter_subset T i)⟩

/-- The viral closure is the intersection of all virally-closed supersets of the
seed: it is the closure map of the Moore family of closed sets. -/
theorem closure_eq_iInter (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) :
    closure C S = ⋂ T ∈ {T : Set V | S ⊆ T ∧ IsViralClosed C T}, T := by
  apply Set.Subset.antisymm
  · apply Set.subset_iInter
    intro T
    apply Set.subset_iInter
    intro hT
    exact closure_le_of_seed_closed C hT.1 hT.2
  · apply Set.iInter_subset_of_subset (closure C S)
    apply Set.iInter_subset_of_subset ⟨subset_closure C S, isViralClosed_closure C S⟩
    exact le_refl _

/-! ## Section 4: The viral path theorem (derivability) -/

/-- An agent `v` is **derivable** from seed `S` under contagion `C` if there is a
finite derivation: `v` is in the seed, or some rule whose premises are all
derivable fires on `v`.  This is the "chain of transmission" view of infection. -/
inductive Derivable (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) : V → Prop
  | seed {v} : v ∈ S → Derivable C S v
  | rule {P v} : (P, v) ∈ C.rules → (∀ p ∈ P, Derivable C S p) → Derivable C S v

/-- The set of derivable agents contains the seed and is virally closed. -/
lemma derivable_seed_closed (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) :
    S ⊆ {v | Derivable C S v} ∧ IsViralClosed C {v | Derivable C S v} := by
  refine ⟨fun v hv => Derivable.seed hv, ?_⟩
  intro v hv
  obtain ⟨P, hP, hPsub⟩ := hv
  exact Derivable.rule hP (fun p hp => hPsub hp)

/-- **Viral path theorem.**  An agent is in the viral closure iff it admits a
finite derivation (a transmission chain) from the seed.  This identifies the
order-theoretic least fixed point with the inductively-generated logical
consequence relation. -/
theorem derivable_iff_mem_closure (C : Contagion V) (S : Set V) (v : V) :
    Derivable C S v ↔ v ∈ closure C S := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    induction h with
    | seed hv => exact subset_closure C S hv
    | rule hP _ ih => exact stepOp_closure_subset C S ⟨_, hP, fun p hp => ih p hp⟩
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨hseed, hclosed⟩ := derivable_seed_closed C S
    exact closure_le_of_seed_closed C hseed hclosed h

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
/-
  HYPOTHESIS (H1): Memetic spread under premise/conclusion rules is governed by a
  monotone operator, so a least fixed point (the "viral closure") exists and is a

  EXPERIMENT: We attempted to show viral closure is a *topological* (Kuratowski)

  empty premises exist.  Both obstructions are made precise as theorems in
  `Thresholds.lean`.  INSIGHT: viral topology is strictly richer than point-set

-/

/-
  # Viral Information Topology — The Topological Dichotomy

  In `Thresholds.lean` we saw that a general (hypergraph) contagion fails the
  Kuratowski axioms `cl ∅ = ∅` and `cl (A ∪ B) = cl A ∪ cl B`.  Here we prove the
  matching *positive* result: a **simple contagion** — one whose every rule has a
  single premise, i.e. ordinary directed-graph reachability — DOES satisfy all the
  Kuratowski axioms.  Its viral closure is therefore a genuine topological
  (Alexandrov) closure.

  This pins down the exact source of non-topological behaviour: **synergy**
  (premises of size ≥ 2).  Memetic spread is topological iff it is pairwise.

  ## Main results

  * `simple_closure_empty` — for a simple contagion `cl ∅ = ∅` (no spontaneous
    generation: a singleton premise can never be satisfied by the empty set).
  * `simple_derivable_union` — a derivation from `A ∪ B` under a simple contagion
    splits: it is a derivation from `A` or a derivation from `B`.
  * `simple_closure_additive` — hence `cl (A ∪ B) = cl A ∪ cl B`.
  * `simple_isKuratowski` — the four Kuratowski closure axioms all hold, so a
    simple viral closure is a topological closure operator.
-/
import Mathlib
import Logic.ViralTopology.Core
import Logic.ViralTopology.Thresholds

open ViralTopology

namespace ViralTopology

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A contagion is **simple** (a "graph contagion") if every rule has exactly one
premise.  This is ordinary directed-graph reachability: an edge `a → c`. -/
def IsSimple (C : Contagion V) : Prop := ∀ r ∈ C.rules, ∃ a, r.1 = {a}

/-! ## Section 1: No spontaneous generation -/

/-- For a simple contagion, the empty set is already virally closed: a singleton
premise can never be a subset of `∅`. -/
theorem simple_stepOp_empty (C : Contagion V) (hC : IsSimple C) :
    stepOp C ∅ = ∅ := by
  ext v
  simp only [stepOp, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  rintro ⟨P, hP, hPsub⟩
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hC (P, v) hP
  have hP1 : P = {a} := ha
  rw [hP1] at hPsub
  exact Set.singleton_subset_iff.1 hPsub

/-- **No spontaneous generation.**  For a simple contagion, `cl ∅ = ∅`. -/
theorem simple_closure_empty (C : Contagion V) (hC : IsSimple C) :
    closure C (∅ : Set V) = ∅ := by
  apply Set.Subset.antisymm
  · apply closure_le_of_seed_closed C (le_refl _)
    rw [simple_stepOp_empty C hC]
  · exact Set.empty_subset _

/-! ## Section 2: Derivations split over unions -/

/-- **Derivation splitting.**  Under a simple contagion, any derivation from a
union `A ∪ B` is entirely a derivation from `A` or entirely from `B`.  (This is
false for synergy rules, where a derivation may genuinely need both sides.) -/
theorem simple_derivable_union (C : Contagion V) (hC : IsSimple C)
    (A B : Set V) (v : V) (h : Derivable C (A ∪ B) v) :
    Derivable C A v ∨ Derivable C B v := by
  induction h with
  | @seed w hw =>
      rcases hw with hw | hw
      · exact Or.inl (Derivable.seed hw)
      · exact Or.inr (Derivable.seed hw)
  | @rule P w hP _ ih =>
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hC (P, w) hP
      have hP1 : P = {a} := ha
      have hamem : a ∈ P := by rw [hP1]; rfl
      rcases ih a hamem with hA | hB
      · refine Or.inl (Derivable.rule hP ?_)
        rw [hP1]; intro p hp
        rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp; subst hp; exact hA
      · refine Or.inr (Derivable.rule hP ?_)
        rw [hP1]; intro p hp
        rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp; subst hp; exact hB

/-! ## Section 3: Finite additivity (Kuratowski) -/

/-- **Finite additivity.**  For a simple contagion the viral closure is additive:
`cl (A ∪ B) = cl A ∪ cl B`. -/
theorem simple_closure_additive (C : Contagion V) (hC : IsSimple C)
    (A B : Set V) :
    closure C (A ∪ B) = closure C A ∪ closure C B := by
  apply Set.Subset.antisymm
  · intro v hv
    have hd : Derivable C (A ∪ B) v :=
      (derivable_iff_mem_closure C (A ∪ B) v).2 hv
    rcases simple_derivable_union C hC A B v hd with hA | hB
    · exact Or.inl ((derivable_iff_mem_closure C A v).1 hA)
    · exact Or.inr ((derivable_iff_mem_closure C B v).1 hB)
  · exact Set.union_subset
      (closure_mono C Set.subset_union_left)
      (closure_mono C Set.subset_union_right)

/-! ## Section 4: The dichotomy -/

/-- **Topological dichotomy.**  For a *simple* (graph) contagion, the viral
closure satisfies all four Kuratowski closure axioms — extensive, idempotent,
`cl ∅ = ∅`, and finitely additive — hence it is a topological (Alexandrov)
closure operator.  Combined with `kuratowski_additivity_fails` and

  * `line_closure_univ` — **total cascade**: on the integer line `ℕ` with rules

  * `closure_empty_ne_empty` — **spontaneous generation**: with an "axiom" rule
    `∅ ↦ v` the empty seed already has a nonempty closure, so `cl ∅ = ∅` (a
    Kuratowski axiom) FAILS.
  * `kuratowski_additivity_fails` — **superadditive synergy**: with a two-premise
    rule `{a,b} ↦ c`, we have `cl (A ∪ B) ≠ cl A ∪ cl B`; finite additivity (a
    Kuratowski axiom) FAILS.

    premises, then any infected agent is already infected by a finite sub-seed.

  proof that viral closure is a *Moore* closure but not a *topological* one.
-/
import Mathlib
import Logic.ViralTopology.Core

open ViralTopology

namespace ViralTopology

variable {V : Type*}

/-! ## Section 1: Monotonicity infrastructure -/

/-- Derivability is monotone in the seed. -/
theorem Derivable.mono (C : Contagion V) {S S' : Set V} (h : S ⊆ S') :
    ∀ {v}, Derivable C S v → Derivable C S' v := by
  intro v hv
  induction hv with
  | seed hmem => exact Derivable.seed (h hmem)
  | rule hP _ ih => exact Derivable.rule hP (fun p hp => ih p hp)

/-- The viral closure is monotone in the seed (restated via derivability). -/
theorem closure_seed_mono (C : Contagion V) {S S' : Set V} (h : S ⊆ S') :
    closure C S ⊆ closure C S' := closure_mono C h

/-! ## Section 2: Total cascade on the line -/

/-- The "line" contagion on `ℕ`: rules `{n} ↦ n+1` for every `n`. -/
def lineContagion : Contagion ℕ := ⟨{r | ∃ n : ℕ, r = ({n}, n + 1)}⟩

/-- Each natural number is derivable from the single seed `{0}`. -/
theorem line_derivable (n : ℕ) : Derivable lineContagion {0} n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Derivable.seed rfl
  | succ k ih =>
      refine Derivable.rule (P := {k}) ⟨k, rfl⟩ ?_
      intro p hp
      rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp
      subst hp
      exact ih

/-- **Total cascade.**  A single seed infects the entire infinite population. -/
theorem line_closure_univ : closure lineContagion {0} = Set.univ := by
  apply Set.eq_univ_of_forall
  intro n
  exact (derivable_iff_mem_closure lineContagion {0} n).1 (line_derivable n)

/-! ## Section 3: Spontaneous generation — `cl ∅ ≠ ∅` -/

/-- An "axiom" contagion on `Fin 1`: the rule `∅ ↦ 0` fires with no premises. -/
def axiomContagion : Contagion (Fin 1) := ⟨{(∅, 0)}⟩

/-- `0` is derivable from the empty seed via the premiseless rule. -/
theorem axiom_derivable_zero : Derivable axiomContagion ∅ 0 := by
  refine Derivable.rule (P := (∅ : Set (Fin 1))) rfl ?_
  intro p hp
  exact absurd hp (by simp)

/-- **Spontaneous generation.**  The Kuratowski axiom `cl ∅ = ∅` FAILS for viral
closure: a premiseless rule makes the empty seed already infectious. -/
theorem closure_empty_ne_empty : closure axiomContagion ∅ ≠ ∅ := by
  intro h
  have : (0 : Fin 1) ∈ closure axiomContagion ∅ :=
    (derivable_iff_mem_closure axiomContagion ∅ 0).1 axiom_derivable_zero
  rw [h] at this
  exact absurd this (by simp)

/-! ## Section 4: Superadditive synergy — failure of finite additivity -/

/-- A synergy contagion on `Fin 3`: the single rule `{0,1} ↦ 2` needs *both*
agents `0` and `1` infected before `2` becomes infected. -/
def synergyContagion : Contagion (Fin 3) := ⟨{(({0, 1} : Set (Fin 3)), 2)}⟩

/-- Under `synergyContagion`, the seed `{0}` infects only `{0}` — the rule never
fires because agent `1` is missing. -/
theorem synergy_closure_singleton_left :
    closure synergyContagion {0} ⊆ {(0 : Fin 3)} := by
  apply closure_le_of_seed_closed synergyContagion (le_refl _)
  rintro v ⟨P, hP, hPsub⟩
  simp only [synergyContagion, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hP
  -- hP : (P, v) = ({0,1}, 2)
  rw [Prod.mk.injEq] at hP
  obtain ⟨hPeq, hveq⟩ := hP
  subst hPeq
  -- hPsub : {0,1} ⊆ {0}; but 1 ∈ {0,1} and 1 ∉ {0}
  exfalso
  have h1 : (1 : Fin 3) ∈ ({0, 1} : Set (Fin 3)) := by right; rfl
  have := hPsub h1
  rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at this
  exact absurd this (by decide)

/-- Symmetric statement: the seed `{1}` infects only `{1}`. -/
theorem synergy_closure_singleton_right :
    closure synergyContagion {1} ⊆ {(1 : Fin 3)} := by
  apply closure_le_of_seed_closed synergyContagion (le_refl _)
  rintro v ⟨P, hP, hPsub⟩
  simp only [synergyContagion, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hP
  rw [Prod.mk.injEq] at hP
  obtain ⟨hPeq, hveq⟩ := hP
  subst hPeq
  exfalso
  have h0 : (0 : Fin 3) ∈ ({0, 1} : Set (Fin 3)) := by left; rfl
  have := hPsub h0
  rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at this
  exact absurd this (by decide)

/-- Under `synergyContagion`, the seed `{0,1}` infects `2`. -/
theorem synergy_derivable_two : Derivable synergyContagion {0, 1} 2 := by
  refine Derivable.rule (P := ({0, 1} : Set (Fin 3))) rfl ?_
  intro p hp
  exact Derivable.seed hp

/-- **Superadditive synergy.**  Finite additivity `cl (A ∪ B) = cl A ∪ cl B` (a
Kuratowski axiom) FAILS for viral closure: combining two seeds can infect agents
that neither seed infects alone. -/
theorem kuratowski_additivity_fails :
    ∃ (W : Type) (C : Contagion W) (A B : Set W),
      closure C (A ∪ B) ≠ closure C A ∪ closure C B := by
  refine ⟨Fin 3, synergyContagion, {0}, {1}, ?_⟩
  intro h
  -- 2 is in the closure of the union but in neither piece
  have hunion : ({0} ∪ {1} : Set (Fin 3)) = {0, 1} := rfl
  have h2mem : (2 : Fin 3) ∈ closure synergyContagion ({0} ∪ {1}) := by
    rw [hunion]
    exact (derivable_iff_mem_closure synergyContagion {0, 1} 2).1 synergy_derivable_two
  rw [h] at h2mem
  rcases h2mem with h2 | h2
  · have := synergy_closure_singleton_left h2
    rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at this
    exact absurd this (by decide)
  · have := synergy_closure_singleton_right h2
    rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at this
    exact absurd this (by decide)

/-! ## Section 5: Finitary spread (compactness) -/

/-
**Viral compactness.**  If every rule has finitely many premises, then any
agent infected by a (possibly infinite) seed is already infected by some finite
sub-seed.  This is the finite-character / compactness property of forward
chaining.
-/
theorem viral_compactness (C : Contagion V) (hfin : ∀ r ∈ C.rules, r.1.Finite)
    (S : Set V) (v : V) (h : Derivable C S v) :
    ∃ S₀ : Set V, S₀ ⊆ S ∧ S₀.Finite ∧ Derivable C S₀ v := by
  induction' h with v hv ih
  · exact ⟨{v}, by simpa using hv, Set.finite_singleton v, Derivable.seed rfl⟩
  · rename_i h₁ h₂ h₃
    choose! f hf₁ hf₂ hf₃ using h₃
    refine ⟨⋃ p ∈ ih, f p, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact Set.iUnion₂_subset fun p hp => hf₁ p hp
    · exact Set.Finite.biUnion (hfin _ h₁) hf₂
    · refine Derivable.rule h₁ ?_
      exact fun p hp =>
        Derivable.mono C (Set.subset_iUnion₂_of_subset p hp (Set.Subset.refl _)) (hf₃ p hp)

  "spontaneous generation" and "synergy" phenomena, which are the interesting
  features of memetic dynamics, not bugs.

  sub-seed as a finite union of the premises' finite witnesses (finite because the
  premise set is finite), then lifts each premise derivation along `Derivable.mono`.
-/

end ViralTopology
